title: Ethiopian Garlic Fish
localName: ቀጭን ዋ አሣ — Nech Shinkurt Asa
community: Ethiopian lakeside towns — the mild garlic fish
author: Chef Haile
desc: Ethiopian Garlic Fish — fish fillets pan-fried in kibbeh with abundant garlic, lemon, fresh jalapeño, and coriander. The mild, garlic-forward fish dish that contrasts with the intensely spiced berbere preparations — light, fresh, and completely accessible.
longDesc: Garlic fish is the refreshing counterpoint to Ethiopia's spiced fish dishes — the kibbeh and abundant garlic produce a golden, aromatic sauce that is significantly milder than berbere-based preparations. Ideal for those who prefer the flavour of kibbeh without the heat of berbere.
steps: Season fish with salt and pepper.
Heat kibbeh in a wide pan over medium-high heat.
Sear fish 3 minutes per side. Remove. Set aside.
In the same pan: add sliced garlic. Cook 2 minutes until golden.
Return fish. Coat in garlic kibbeh. Cook 1 more minute.
chefTips: The garlic must be sliced, not minced — it needs to caramelise into golden slices.
Remove fish before cooking garlic — garlic burns faster than fish cooks.
commonMistakes: Over-cooking garlic — burned garlic is bitter.
cookingScience: Sliced garlic caramelises more evenly than minced — the larger pieces have more surface area for Maillard browning while the interior remains sweet and mild. Minced garlic, with its much smaller pieces, burns on the exterior before the interior has cooked, producing acrid compounds.
healthBenefits: Garlic is powerfully antimicrobial and antioxidant.
culturalNote: Garlic fish is the gentle face of Ethiopian fish cooking — for guests who want the kibbeh richness without the berbere heat. It is the dish that makes Ethiopian food accessible to those who are new to it.
